entries.reason: Old-generation marking is stop-the-world; concurrent SATB marking and termination are absent.
Region evacuation and sparse-first ordering exist, but the complete highest-garbage selection contract has not been validated and remains partial debt.
Side bitmaps exist, but concurrent mark-state safety cannot be established until concurrent old-generation marking exists.
Production T2 has SSA definitions, block parameters, and dominance tests; reviewed requirement-to-test traceability is missing after legacy-test removal.
Production T2 has explicit CFG edges, block arguments, terminators, and verifier tests; the effect-ordering and aliasing clause still needs focused audit.
The T2 builder still declines unsupported expanded forms; there is no proof or implementation matrix for every ANSI special operator.
The verifier omits opcode type schemas and effect ordering and is not run after every pass in debug builds.
Production guards carry FrameState and deoptimization metadata with verifier and live-state tests; exact requirement-to-test mapping still needs review.
IR source positions are commonly zero, block parameters carry none, and full file/line/column/macro-depth reconstruction is absent.
Production tests independently exercise invocation-count and loop-heat promotion to T2; reviewed requirement-to-test mapping is missing.
Production tests exercise synchronous T1 availability and continued T1 execution during background T2 compilation; reviewed traceability is missing.
Production live-OSR tests exercise T1 execution until atomic T2 publication and transition; reviewed traceability is missing.
Production tests prove unsupported T2 compilation retains the working T1 entry; reviewed requirement-to-test mapping is missing.
Required threshold environment names and defaults are implemented; exact mandated aliases and defaults need focused coverage.
The production queue is bounded and increments a drop counter without blocking, but lacks a deterministic overflow regression.
Type/range inference and declaration-driven guard removal are tested; full declaration ingress and lattice breadth still need focused audit.
Inlining limits exist, but source NOTINLINE and OPTIMIZE SPEED 0 policies are not propagated to the production inliner.
Escape analysis is limited and no lowering turns non-escaping allocations into stack allocations.
LICM is implemented and unit-tested but is not scheduled in the production T2 pass pipeline.
Production DCE tests cover pure dead values, effects, and deoptimization state; reviewed requirement-to-test mapping is missing.
Production folding and strength reduction do not implement full Common Lisp numeric contagion and rounding semantics.
Dominator-based duplicate-guard elimination exists, but the exact nil-guard contract lacks a focused regression.
Guard deoptimization reconstructs interpreter state, but requested deoptimization at arbitrary GC safepoints is absent.
Production stress tests exercise OSR/deoptimization state and moving heap roots across GC-safe transitions; reviewed traceability is missing.
Unsupported lowering is represented and rejected, but an end-to-end unlowered-node installation-abort test is still needed.
The x86 backend has SysV call machinery and XMM floating-point emission; mixed ABI and SSE2 baseline coverage needs consolidation.
Production regalloc2 tests cover GPR/XMM classes, spills, call constraints, and FrameState locations; reviewed traceability is missing.
Production tests cover per-safepoint stack maps and rejection of missing maps at installation; reviewed traceability is missing.
Executable memory is finalized RW-to-RX, but there is no live atomic patch-site API or architecture barrier protocol.
Production generic, type-check, and slot-access sites are not all backed by per-call-site inline caches.
There is no production per-site monomorphic, bounded-polymorphic, and megamorphic state machine.
Production inline-cache entry publication does not exist, so atomic concurrent transitions are unimplemented.
Global generic-cache invalidation exists, but compiled per-site generic, type, and slot cache invalidation does not.
There is no production megamorphic per-site hash fallback or required latency benchmark.
Counters wrap, the back-edge counter is aggregate rather than per edge, and deoptimization resets it, violating monotonicity.
Scheduler reads are relaxed atomic loads and bounded receiver profiles exist; current concurrent-read coverage is missing.
Production tests independently exercise invocation and back-edge promotion thresholds; reviewed requirement-to-test mapping is missing.
